description: The old bull of the brutes. Whole warbands have broken against shoulders wider than their shield-wall.
lore: There was an age here with enough people in it, and enough agreement between them, to put a shield-wall in a field and walk it forward in step. Sit with that fact by itself for a moment; it is a larger thing to know about this country's past than anything the animal ever did. Then note that the wall is the part that broke. The bull is out there yet, old past any counting, uninterested. It does not grind its tusks and has not needed to for longer than anyone can account for, and [[monsters/gray_brute|the young ones]] file theirs off rather than come and ask. So no one asks. It moves when it wants the sun.

[[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] will tell you about that field. Hearn will tell you about it at length: the frost in the ground, the order the flanks went in, the sound a shield-wall makes at the moment it stops being a line and becomes people. He was not there — it was long before him — and he has every yard of it from those who were, and he can hold a fire for a whole evening with it, generous and exact and warm. It is not the story anybody sat down for. They sit down because Hearn went into the mountain with a party and came out of it by himself, and because he once said, of the inside, that it asked politely, and has said nothing since. So he gives them Tuskmaul. He gives them Tuskmaul every single time, and they take it, and they come back next week and take it again.
gm_notes: The one restrained sentence of history: organised warbands existed, once, which is a real fact about the lost ages and is not elaborated further. Hearn is the point of the record — the old bull is his safe war story, offered every time in place of the one his listeners actually want. Hints nothing new about the cave (B7 stays where it is); it only shows the shape of a man refusing.
